digest.component_or_area: completion verifier budget and verdict persistence
propositions: Step budget defaults (8 per criterion, 48 floor, 480 clamp) cause legitimate validation to exhaust and false-fail criteria that are merely unproven-within-budget, driving operators to attestation-laundering.

Budget sizing ignores the evidence surface (child ticket traversal costs 5-10 requests per epic child) leading to undersized allocations for multi-AC epics; a separate runaway guard (tool_calls_limit, loop detection) already prevents tool use abuse, so the tight budget adds false failures without safety gain.

Re-verification of the same criterion across multiple runs re-proves identical criteria from scratch (~10 min per cycle) due to absence of cross-run verdict caching, wasting compute on already-validated PASS outcomes.

The budget formula must scale with (criteria_count × per_criterion + direct_children × child_traversal + fixed_overhead) and be bounded by a 960-step clamp to accommodate 20+ AC epics, with cached PASS verdicts seeded into subsequent runs via a scoped content fingerprint keyed on criterion text and file impact blob SHAs rather than whole-tree SHA.

Cache entries must be invalidated when criterion text or in-scope file content changes (blob SHA rotation) but remain valid across unrelated commits and worktree refreshes; ref-pinned verification must bind fingerprints to the verified commit, not HEAD, to prevent illegitimate reuse in close workflows.
